# visionary_uptime_location (Resource)

An uptime location: a place checks run from, served by a host agent started with VISIONARY_AGENT_LOCATION and the location's key. Visionary shows the key once, when the location is made, so it is kept in the state as secret. Needs an admin key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A place to run checks from: a VPS in Frankfurt running
#   VISIONARY_AGENT_LOCATION=frankfurt-vps VISIONARY_KEY=<key> visionary-agent
resource "visionary_uptime_location" "frankfurt" {
  name = "frankfurt-vps"
}

output "frankfurt_location_key" {
  value     = visionary_uptime_location.frankfurt.key
  sensitive = true
}

# Down only when most of its locations fail.
resource "visionary_uptime_check" "shop" {
  name          = "Shop"
  url           = "https://shop.example.com"
  locations     = ["server", visionary_uptime_location.frankfurt.name]
  location_rule = "majority"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name checks use in their locations, e.g. frankfurt-vps: 1–48 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The location's name.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The location key (VISIONARY_KEY for its runner). Empty for an imported location.
- `key_prefix` (String) The visible start of the key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is the location's name. An imported location's key stays empty:
# Visionary only shows it when the location (or a new key) is made.
terraform import visionary_uptime_location.example frankfurt-vps
```
